To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
some anti-HCV/E1/E2 antibodies can induce conformation changes in HCV/E2, and these changes may affect the ability of other antibodies to inhibit the binding of HCV to target cells.

the binding of HCV E2 to its target is less prone of inhibition by some antibody clone, that this can explain why high titers of anti-HCV E2 antibodies are not protective, and that information on the interactions among antibody clones can be relevant to understanding virus-host interactions and developing more effective vaccine strategies.

human recombinant Fab fragments against HCV/E1 glycoprotein can modify conformation of HCV/E1 and that this modification can reduce the ability of some anti-HCV/E1 Fab fragments to neutralize the binding of HCV to target cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the human antibody response against the hepatitis C virus E1/E2 complex and its role in the protection from infection.
the study of the immune response to hepatitis C virus E-2 (HCV-2) glycoproteins.
the study of the human immune responses against HCV/E1 and HCV/E2 and their role in the pathogenesis and the prevention of HCV infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
some antibody clones, even if not directly neutralizing, may be relevant to the immune response against HVC/E2.
the NOB activity of the human anti-HCV/E1/E2 immune response is highly heterogeneous and can be modulated by the binding of some anti-HCV/E glycoprotein antibody clones.
the presence of NOB activity in an antibody is not sufficient for the antibody to protect from infection, but that it is a good predictor of the ability of an antibody to protect from reinfection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the human immune response can be divided into two groups: one that neutralizes the virus and another one that modulates the virus.
we generated recombinant human antibody fragments with a high affinity to HCV E2 glycoproteins, which did not neutralize the binding to target cells.

we identified a novel human antibody fragment against HCV/E1/E2 that has the ability to modulate NOB activity of other anti-HCV antibodies, and that this activity is related to the conformational changes induced on the HCV/E1-E2 heterodimer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the context of the immune response against HVC/E2, the NOB activity of antibodies can be modulated by the binding of other antibodies to distinct sites of the same antigen.
the binding of some anti-HCV/E1/E2 antibodies can induce conformation changes in HCV/E1/E1/E2 glycoprotein that reduce the ability of other antibodies to neutralize binding.
the conformation of the HCV/E2 envelope glycoprotein is modified by binding of some anti-HCV/E1 and anti-E2 antibodies.
